ra: Silouan was an Athonite monk of St Panteleimon's; charter member of the modern Athonite eldership.
Joseph the Hesychast was a foundational 20th-c. Athonite elder whose disciples renewed Athos.
Paisios was among the most prominent modern Athonite elders.
Porphyrios was an Athonite elder of Kavsokalyvia.
Sophrony lived on Athos as a hesychast disciple of Silouan before founding his Essex monastery.
Nicholas II is the principal of the Romanov passion-bearers glorified in 2000.
Empress Alexandra was glorified among the Royal Martyrs in 2000.
Tsarevich Alexei was glorified among the Royal Martyrs in 2000.
As passion-bearers (strastoterptsy) the Romanovs are venerated for accepting death in imitation of Christ's passion; passion-bearing is explicitly a reception of Christ's Passion, not deification.
Sophrony was the personal disciple and biographer of Silouan the Athonite, whose teaching he transmitted.
Nikodemos was an Athonite monk whose life embodied hesychast monasticism.
As co-compiler of the Philokalia he transmitted the hesychast doctrine of the uncreated light/noetic prayer.
Theophan translated the Philokalia into Russian, transmitting the hesychast tradition of inner light and the prayer of the heart.
Theophan's principal teaching concerned unceasing prayer and the prayer of the heart.
Ignatius's central work, On the Prayer of Jesus, teaches the practice of the Jesus Prayer.
Ignatius was a monastic reformer whose Arena systematizes patristic ascetic life.
Silouan's teaching is firmly within the hesychast experience of grace and the uncreated light.
Silouan taught the practice of the Jesus Prayer and prayer for the whole world.
Joseph the Hesychast taught noetic prayer and the experience of divine grace in the hesychast tradition.
Paisios taught the Jesus Prayer and was a renowned counselor on the spiritual life.
Porphyrios was widely venerated for charismatic gifts of healing and spiritual insight.
Sophrony's theology of personhood and the vision of the uncreated light continues the Palamite hesychast tradition.
John of Kronstadt was venerated in his lifetime for numerous miracles of healing.
John of Kronstadt belongs to the same Russian wonderworker tradition as Seraphim of Sarov.
Nektarios of Aegina is one of the most popular modern Greek healing wonderworkers.
Luke (Voino-Yasenetsky) was both a surgeon and venerated healer; patron of physicians and the sick.
As a physician-saint Luke continues the tradition of the unmercenary healers such as Panteleimon.
Matrona of Moscow is venerated principally for healing and consolation.
Matrona stands in the Russian wonderworker lineage exemplified by Seraphim of Sarov.
John of Shanghai and San Francisco was venerated as an ascetic wonderworker and healer in the diaspora.
John lived a strict ascetic-monastic episcopate.
Elizabeth founded and led the Martha and Mary Convent, embodying the monastic-diaconal life.
As a new-martyr she is venerated for accepting death in imitation of Christ; martyrdom as reception of Christ's Passion, not deification.
Maria of Paris is venerated as a new-martyr who died at Ravensbruck serving Christ in the persecuted; martyrdom as reception of Christ's Passion.
Maria was a professed nun who reconceived monasticism as active social charity.
Nikolai Velimirovic, 'the Serbian Chrysostom', was a major preacher and theological writer.
Justin Popovic was a leading 20th-c. dogmatic theologian of the Orthodox Church.
Justin Popovic was a younger associate and spiritual heir of Nikolai Velimirovic within the Serbian Orthodox revival.
